newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Eurorands hearten S.Africa, investors nurse losses.
newsitem.headline: Eurorands hearten S.Africa, investors nurse losses.

text.p: A rash of Eurorand bond issues, which saw a further 350 million rand hit the market via two new issues on Friday, has heartened the local South African bond market.

But dealers and bankers said demand for the new wave of rand paper was being driven primarily by a desire among existing investors to roll over their losses rather than any new confidence in South African debt.
"I don't see it as being a natural for investors to rush to," said Roger Bates, director at Deutsche Bank in London, pointing to the weak rand and a sharply inverted domestic yield curve.

"But people who bought when the rand was in the 3.60s (against the dollar) are reinvesting rather than taking the currency hit. They're not entirely happy about reinvesting but it is the lesser of two evils."
The rand leapt into the spotlight on the Eurobond market at the end of 1995 with a total of 26 issues launched between September 1995 and February 1996.

Then the market turned sour as the currency started its lengthy descent which saw it shed 29 percent against the dollar in 1996, battered by political and economic uncertainty and persistent speculation about the ending of exchange controls.
The rand was last trading around 4.67 on the dollar.

Mike Lamont, director of fixed interest at Standard Corporate and Merchant Bank in Johannesburg, agreed rollovers were a large factor in the raft of new paper but said the very existence of such issues was helping the market mood.
There was also some impact in the local market as some of the issues were swapped into medium-dated local issues, although such business was fairly small-scale.
"Some of it is filtering through to the (local) bond market through the swap desk but the impact is more on sentiment than anything else," said Lamont.
The benchmark R150 issue was last yielding 15.74 percent, down from 15.90 on Thursday, having broken through the 16 percent level earlier in the week.
Friday's new issues featured WestLB Finance Curacao with a three-year 200 million rand bond and Eurofima with a one-year bond for 150 million rand.
These came hard on the heels of a General Electric Capital Corp three-year 200 million rand bond on Thursday, and several other issues since the new year.
Dealers said further Eurorand issues could be in the pipeline with around one billion rand worth of existing Eurobonds due to mature in coming weeks.
